title: Rush the Payroll Handoff
subtitle: A moved start compresses the window
scenario: The start moved earlier, compressing the payroll window - there is less lead time to hit the first cycle. Hand off enrollment to the Payroll Specialist, flag it as a rush so it is not queued behind routine work, and keep the pay class from the profile.
input: Task: payroll for hire H-4022 (owner Payroll Specialist, due SD-3). Pay class from the profile: Non-exempt / Hourly. Because the start moved earlier, the enrollment window is tight - flag this handoff as rush so Payroll prioritizes it to make the first pay cycle.
instructions: Record who the enrollment is sent to.
Set the pay class from the role profile.
Flag the priority as rush (the compressed window).
Validate to mint the payroll handoff record.

fields.label: Sent to
fields.explain: Enrollment goes to the Payroll Specialist, who owns the payroll system.

fields.label: Pay class
fields.explain: The pay class comes from the role profile, not a guess - Logistics Coordinator is Non-exempt / Hourly.

fields.label: Priority
fields.explain: The moved start compressed the window; flagging rush is what keeps enrollment ahead of the first pay cycle.

successMessage: Payroll rushed. The compressed window is flagged so enrollment still makes the first cycle.

sections.title: A moved start moves risk
sections.body: Payroll was already the earliest deadline. Moving the start earlier squeezes it further. The same handoff now needs a priority flag so it does not sit in a routine queue.

sections.title: Rush is a signal, not a panic
sections.body: Flagging rush tells Payroll where the real deadline pressure is. It is how a compressed window becomes an explicit priority rather than a silent risk.

sections.title: The class is still governed
sections.body: Speed does not change the pay class - it still comes from the role profile. Rushing the timing must not mean guessing the classification.

sections.title: What you produce here
sections.body: A rushed payroll handoff record. The tracker still shows it done, but the priority is captured for audit.

takeaway.heading: Payroll rushed
points: You sent enrollment to the Payroll Specialist with the profile's pay class.
The compressed window is flagged rush so it beats the first pay cycle.
Speed did not change the governed pay class.
The priority is captured for audit, and the branch is done.
The workflow can now flag time pressure explicitly when a start moves.
